Track 14

Contact center

Place a voice model beside the queue, the recording, and the human who still owns the call.

Start this track

  1. 01Contact center voice AI: the ASR, TTS, and LLM loopThe phone system owns the call. A voice bot is a treatment on that call: something listens, something decides, something speaks, and a human can still be offered the leg. This room draws the loop, a latency budget you can argue about without inventing an industry SLA, and barge-in that stops audio the caller did not hear.270 min
  2. 02AI agents in the contact centerA virtual agent talks to the caller. Agent assist talks to the human who still owns the call. This room names the bridges vendors actually publish — Webex, Amazon Connect, Google CCAI through the Webex connector, and the Microsoft pieces those pages name — and it refuses tenant click-paths, word-error rates, and millisecond budgets this lab did not measure.240 min
  3. 03AI in the contact center ecosystemA virtual agent talks to the caller. Assist talks to the human. A summary is a draft the human still has to read. Quality management scores the contact later. A forecast predicts volume and handle time. None of those jobs is the phone system, and none of them is allowed to invent a refund. This room names what Webex, Google CCAI, Amazon Connect, and Dynamics 365 actually print about those jobs, retrieved 2026-10-14.240 min
  4. 04Responsible AI and data privacy for voiceA voice bot hears account numbers, records a waveform, and writes a transcript into a log that outlives the call. This room separates redaction, consent, and retention, and it refuses to invent a PCI scope or a retention period the lab did not read.240 min
  5. 05Build a RAG voice agent for a contact centerOne design, end to end: a caller asks a question, a retriever packs evidence, a model may request a tool, and a human queue still exists. This room is the architecture, the eval plan, and the rollout. It does not invent a dial plan, a word-error rate, or a millisecond promise.300 min

The citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date.</p></aside><p>The phone system owns the call. A voice bot is a treatment on that call: something listens, something decides, something speaks, and a human can still be offered the leg. This room draws the loop, a latency budget you can argue about without inventing an industry SLA, and barge-in that stops audio the caller did not hear.</p><h3>01Executive summary</h3><ul><li>Two shapes: a cascade (ASR → text model → TTS) and a speech-to-speech session. OpenAI’s Realtime getting-started guide describes a model that works directly with audio, keeps conversation state, can call tools, and is aimed at barge-in and turn-taking. That is one vendor’s product, not the definition of a contact center. [cite:1]</li><li>Barge-in is the caller talking over playback. The conversations guide says to stop playback, cancel the response, and truncate the unplayed audio with <code>conversation.item.truncate</code> so the model’s history matches what was heard. [cite:2]</li><li>The VAD guide’s sample <code>server_vad</code> session includes <code>threshold</code> 0.5, <code>prefix_padding_ms</code> 300, <code>silence_duration_ms</code> 500, <code>create_response</code> true, and <code>interrupt_response</code> true. Those are example fields, not a millisecond SLA for your queues. [cite:3]</li><li>Do not execute a tool on a partial transcript. Consent still sits in the host, as in T4. A side effect during an interruption is how a “no” becomes a refund.</li><li>Containment is not resolution. A latency budget is a worksheet. This room does not publish a universal millisecond number. Measure the edge you ship.</li></ul><aside class="callout note"><h3>Why it matters for the lab engineer</h3><p>Voice is where a lab habit becomes a caller’s silence. Interviewers ask where the milliseconds go and what happens when the caller interrupts. The honest answer names the hops, cites the controls you have actually read, and refuses a fake “under 300 ms end to end” that no document in this room states. CUCM, Webex, and UCCE still own the route. The model does not become a second ACD.</p></aside><h3>02Architecture</h3><p>Caller audio, a turn detector, recognition, the model, synthesis, barge-in, and the ACD if you transfer.</p><p>Diagram: Seven stages from caller audio to the ACD</p><ul><li>The ACD is outside the model. Transfer is a route.</li><li>Barge-in is a loop back to the media layer, not a prompt adjective.</li><li>ASR may be a separate hop or folded into a speech-to-speech model. Say which one you shipped.</li></ul><h3>Mermaid source for a later redraw</h3><pre><code>flowchart LR

  V --> A["ASR or audio model"]
  A --> M["Decision"]
  M --> T["TTS or audio out"]
  T --> C
  C -.->|barge-in| V
  M --> Q["ACD transfer"]</code></pre><p>Playback starts, the caller talks over it, playback stops, unplayed audio is truncated.</p><p>Diagram: Caller, media, ASR, model, TTS with an interruption</p><p>The diagram shows a cascade because the hops are easy to point at. A speech-to-speech API collapses ASR, the language model, and some of the turn-taking into one session. You still have a media edge, a tool boundary, and a phone system. Collapsing hops does not delete the ACD. [cite:1]</p><h3>03Deep dive</h3><p>Start from the object the caller experiences: silence, then a voice, then maybe an interruption, then either an answer or a human. Everything else is a hop you can time. If you cannot name the hop, you will “tune the prompt” for a problem that was a playback buffer.</p><h3>Cascade and speech-to-speech</h3><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th></th><th>Cascade</th><th>Speech-to-speech session</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>What crosses the model boundary</td><td>Text from ASR, text toward TTS</td><td>Audio, in the Realtime guide’s description, plus tool calls [cite:1]</td></tr><tr><td>Where you read the words</td><td>The ASR transcript and the model’s text</td><td>The conversations guide names <code>conversation.item.truncate</code> because the server can emit audio the client has not played. [cite:2] [cite:3]</td></tr><tr><td>Barge-in</td><td>Your media server must stop TTS and tell the dialog what was played</td><td>The conversations guide: VAD cancels the response; you truncate unplayed audio [cite:2]</td></tr><tr><td>Failure you can see</td><td>ASR error versus model error versus TTS error are different logs</td><td>A single session can hide which sub-hop was late unless you still time the edges</td></tr><tr><td>Who owns the call</td><td>The ACD, in both columns</td><td>The ACD, in both columns</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>The Realtime getting-started guide says to use that API when the interaction should feel conversational, and it names barge-in, low first-audio latency, natural turn-taking, and realtime tool use as the reasons. “Low” is the guide’s adjective. It does not publish a contact-center end-to-end millisecond budget in the passage this room relies on. Do not invent one. [cite:1]</p><aside class="callout note"><h3>Gotcha</h3><p>A speech-to-speech demo that never places a PSTN or Webex call has not tested the contact center. The model session is the middle. Jitter, codec, and the queue are still there. Vendor pages fetched 2026-10-14 name three families you can point at without opening a tenant: Cisco Webex AI Agent, integrated from AI Agent Studio with voice and digital channels for Webex Contact Center Enterprise, CCE, and CCX; Amazon Connect Customer AI agents, including real-time assistance in the agent workspace, with Amazon Q in Connect described as a generative assistant built on Amazon Bedrock and as an evolution of Amazon Connect Wisdom; and a Google CCAI connector that Webex documents for Webex CCE, Unified CCE, and Packaged CCE. [cite:10] [cite:11] [cite:12] [cite:13] Which of those is installed on your edge is a tenant fact. The jitter and codec rows below stay measurements. This sentence only names the product families the fetched pages describe.</p></aside><h3>Turns</h3><p>Endpointing is the decision that the caller has finished. Too eager, and you cut them off. Too late, and they think the line is dead and start talking over you, which is the latency-spike incident wearing an acoustic mask. OpenAI’s VAD guide describes server-side voice activity detection that uses periods of silence to chunk audio. The sample session in that guide sets a threshold, a prefix padding, and a silence duration, and it sets <code>interrupt_response</code> and <code>create_response</code> for conversation mode. Quote the sample as a sample. Then measure your own callers. A billing verification needs a longer silence than a yes/no menu. The guide also describes an eagerness control in some modes. Confirm it on the page you ship against. [cite:3]</p><p>Partial hypotheses are not turns. ASR often emits unstable text before the endpoint. A refund tool that fires on “refund every…” while the caller is still saying “…thing except the last one” is an incident. Wait for the endpoint you defined. Then, if the act is a side effect, take consent in the host the way T4 describes. The MCP revision pinned in that room does not become optional because the user is speaking.</p><h3>Barge-in</h3><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Step</th><th>What must be true</th><th>If you skip it</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Detect speech during playback</td><td>VAD or your media server marks the start</td><td>The bot keeps talking. The caller talks louder. You log a “overlap” and learn nothing.</td></tr><tr><td>Stop local playback immediately</td><td>The speaker goes quiet</td><td>The caller hears the rest of a sentence you are about to retract.</td></tr><tr><td>Cancel the in-flight response</td><td>The session stops generating</td><td>Tokens keep arriving into a buffer you already abandoned. [cite:2]</td></tr><tr><td>Truncate unplayed audio</td><td><code>conversation.item.truncate</code> with the audio the caller actually heard, in the Realtime guide</td><td>The model believes it finished a sentence the caller never heard, and the next turn is nonsense. [cite:2]</td></tr><tr><td>Do not run a new tool until the new turn is endpointed and consented</td><td>Host rule</td><td>An interruption that sounds like “no” still executes “yes.”</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>The conversations guide is explicit that the server can produce audio faster than realtime, which is why truncate exists: audio may already have been sent to the client and not yet played. That is the bug people misread as “the model is rude.” The model’s context and the caller’s ears diverged. Truncation is how you repair the context. It is not a prompt. [cite:2]</p><aside class="callout note"><h3>Tip</h3><p>Log two clocks: generated-audio duration and played-audio duration. The gap is what truncate must report. If you only log the transcript, you cannot explain the next confused turn. [cite:15]</td></tr><tr><td>Model, first token or first audio</td><td>The language or speech model</td><td>No millisecond SLA is on the pricing page. If ASR time is flat and the tool row grew, you do not retune silence_duration_ms. If the cap’s finish reason is max_output_tokens and the caller heard half a sentence, you are looking at the cap, not at the microphone. [cite:4]</p><h3>What the bot is allowed to do</h3><p>Four outcomes, the same as T2: identify, authenticate, answer from an allowed source, or transfer. Containment counts calls that never reached a human. Resolution counts problems that stayed fixed. A bot that hangs up after a wrong answer is highly contained and unresolved. Track repeats and the reason codes on transfers. This room does not publish an ACD catalog. Log pack miss, caller asked, and policy refusal.</p><p>The handoff packet is the difference between a transfer and a restart. Include the intent, which identity checks already passed, what was promised, and the transcript span. Do not include a full card number. PCI SSC’s page, fetched 2026-10-14, says the standard is for entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder data or sensitive authentication data, and that a QSA assesses. This room does not assign scope. [cite:16] The packet is a tool result the desktop shows. It is not a paragraph the model improvises at the moment of transfer, because that paragraph can hallucinate a promise the human then has to keep.</p><p>Authentication prompts on a voice line are easy to over-collect. Ask only for the fields the tool schema allows. A partial ASR of a secret is still a secret in your logs. Redact before the trace. T5’s retention warning applies twice, because audio is harder to anonymize than a sentence.</p><h3>A Tuesday spike, told as hops</h3><p>Imagine time-to-first-audio moving from a range the team had accepted into a range that makes callers talk over the bot. The VAD sample is still at the guide’s example silence. ASR endpoint time has not moved. The new deploy added a “be thorough” tool that looks up the account, then a second tool that drafts a note, then the reply. The trace shows two <code>execute_tool</code> spans before any audio. The finish reason on the reply is sometimes the output cap, so the caller hears a fragment and interrupts. The fragment is exactly the failure mode of a cap that counts tokens the caller never hears. [cite:4] [cite:5]</p><p>The wrong first move is to set silence duration to a smaller number because the sample used 500 and “faster must be smaller.” That clips the next caller who is reading an account number. The right move is to take the note-drafting tool off the hot path, keep barge-in, and raise the output cap only if the finish reason says the cap fired. Then add a golden case whose pass rule is “at most one tool before first audio on this intent.” T5 fails the build if the thoroughness tool returns. The voice stack did not regress. The agent loop did. Saying that cleanly is the whole job of the budget worksheet.</p><p>A second spike looks similar and is not. Played audio is short, generated audio is long, and the next turn answers a question the caller did not hear. Truncate was never sent, or it was sent with the generated length instead of the played length. The conversations guide’s reason for the event is this gap. Fix the client. Do not retrain a model to “stop mentioning” a sentence that is still in its context. [cite:2]</p><p>Handoff belongs in the same story. If the spike ends in a transfer, the human’s first two seconds need the packet: intent, what authentication already passed, the fact that no refund tool ran, and the transcript span of the interruption. A model-written summary that says “customer agreed to a credit” is a new incident glued to the latency incident. Assemble the packet from tool results. The desktop renders it. The ACD routes. You do not need a tenant menu to specify those fields. This room does not reproduce one.</p><p>Codec and jitter sit under every row and are easy to forget because they are not in the model request. A browser demo on a laptop plays PCM with almost no buffer. A queue plays a telephony codec through a jitter buffer that exists to hide packet loss. If you measure time-to-first-audio only in the browser, you have measured a different system. Place at least one call through the same edge the caller will use before you publish a budget, and record which hop grew. The product families on the fetched pages are Webex AI Agent (voice and digital, including the Webex Connect channels named in T7-R02), Amazon Connect Customer AI agents with Q in Connect, and Google CCAI through the Webex connector. The Q CLI reference lists assistant types including SELF_SERVICE, ANSWER_RECOMMENDATION, and CASE_SUMMARIZATION. The CCAI article lists data centers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Frankfurt, Australia, Japan, Singapore, and Canada, and it says Agent Answers is not applicable to the Webex Contact Center solution. Those are names and a region list, not a buffer setting. This room does not publish that edge’s jitter-buffer setting. Time the call before you publish a budget. Refuse a millisecond you did not time on the path you will ship. [cite:10] [cite:12] [cite:14]</p><p>Barge-in has a cousin in half-duplex systems that never interrupt cleanly because the media server mixes both sides into one recording. The caller hears echo, the VAD hears the bot, and you cancel your own playback. If speech-start events fire while you are the one talking, you are detecting yourself. Gate VAD on “playback is active and the far end has energy,” and test it with a recording of your own TTS, not only with a quiet room. That test is local. It does not require a model key. It requires honesty about which audio is the caller.</p><p>When you brief an on-call engineer, give them the worksheet and the two clocks, not a slogan. Played milliseconds against generated milliseconds tells them whether truncate ran. Tool-span time tells them whether the agent loop ate the turn. ASR time tells them whether the recognizer moved. If all three are flat and only the jitter buffer grew, the model is innocent and the edge is not. That sentence is the difference between a voice incident and a prompt incident, and it is the sentence this room exists to make sayable.</p><h3>04Walk-through</h3><p>The bot is speaking a refund policy. A leaf ends in a citation, or in a sentence that refuses to invent the number.</p><h3>L0 · Who owns the call?</h3><p>The phone system. The model is a treatment. Transfer is a route, not a token.</p><h3>L1 · Cascade versus speech-to-speech?</h3><p>Cascade: ASR text, a language model, TTS. Speech-to-speech, in OpenAI’s Realtime guide: the model works with audio, keeps state, and can call tools. The guide names barge-in and turn-taking as reasons to use it. “Low latency” there is an adjective, not a number I will repeat as an SLA. [cite:1]</p><h3>L2 · What does barge-in require?</h3><p>Stop playback, cancel the response, truncate unplayed audio so the model’s history matches the caller’s ears. The conversations guide names <code>conversation.item.truncate</code> because the server can emit audio faster than it is played. [cite:2]</p><h3>L1 · What is the VAD sample allowed to mean?</h3><p>An example: threshold 0.5, prefix padding 300 ms, silence 500 ms, interrupt_response true. Measure your own endpoint. Do not engrave 500 on the queue. [cite:3]</p><h3>L3 · Why not fire a tool on a partial?</h3><p>The hypothesis is unstable. “Refund every” can still become “everything except the last order.” Wait for the endpoint, then consent if there is a side effect. [cite:6]</p><h3>L3 · Barge-in during consent?</h3><p>Cancel the pending tool. A “no” spoken over the confirm must not become a second “yes.” Log tool count zero for that turn so T5 can grade it.</p><h3>L4 · Which latency numbers are cited and which are not?</h3><p>The VAD sample’s 300 and 500 are cited as examples. This room does not publish an end-to-end millisecond target or a telephony word-error rate. The 2022 Whisper LibriSpeech test-clean range is 2.5 to 6.7 and is read speech. Output caps are cited as fields that include non-visible tokens, which can end a reply before audible audio. [cite:3] [cite:4] [cite:15]</p><h3>L4 · Containment versus resolution?</h3><p>Containment: no human took the call. Resolution: the problem stayed fixed. Report repeats beside containment. This room does not publish an ACD reason-code catalog. Log pack miss, caller asked, and policy refusal.</p><h3>L5 · What would you redesign, and what stops you?</h3><p>I would time every hop and refuse a single “voice latency” alert. I would truncate on every interruption. What stops a looser design is a model context that describes audio the caller never heard, and a tool that moves money during the word “no.” This room does not publish a universal millisecond target. [cite:2]</p><h3>Leaf · What do you log besides the transcript?</h3><p>Played milliseconds versus generated milliseconds. The gap is the truncate argument. [cite:2]</p><h3>Leaf · What is in the handoff packet?</h3><p>Intent, identity checks already done, promises already made, transcript span. Not a full card number. This room does not assign PCI scope. A QSA does. [cite:16]</p><h3>Leaf · interrupt_response false means what, in the VAD guide?</h3><p>An ongoing response is not automatically cancelled when VAD hears speech. Know which value you shipped. The sample sets it true. [cite:3]</p><h3>Leaf · Where does MCP still apply?</h3><p>Tools are still host-executed with consent. Speaking does not waive revision 2025-11-25. [cite:6]</p><h3>09Lab</h3><p>No audio vendor and no API key. Use a timer and the tracer for the tool half. Do not place a real customer call.</p><ol><li>Draw cascade and speech-to-speech on one page. Circle the ACD in both.</li><li>Fill the budget worksheet with TODO in every cell you have not measured. Put 300 and 500 only in the VAD-example row, labeled example. [cite:3]</li><li>Write the five barge-in steps. Say when the endpoint fires.</li><li>Draft a handoff packet with no PAN and no invented promise.</li><li>Write one T5 case: barge-in during consent, expected tool count zero.</li></ol><h3>10Quiz</h3><p>Multiple choice</p><h3>Q1. Who owns the call?</h3><ol><li>The language model.</li><li>The phone system. False would let that response continue. The sample sets true. [cite:3]</p><p>Short answer</p><h3>Q12. Why is a partial transcript not a tool call?</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>It can still change. Side effects wait for an endpoint and for host consent. Speaking does not waive the tool loop. [cite:6]</p><h3>11Audio slots</h3><p>Silent placeholder. Do not describe it as a recorded lesson.</p><p>Overview · 3–5 min</p><h3>Transcript prompt</h3><p>Name the owner of the call. <article class="lesson" id="14-p-t7r02" data-panel="lesson" data-school="14" data-title="AI agents in the contact center" data-search="14-p-t7r02 ai agents in the contact center a virtual agent talks to the caller. agent assist talks to the human who still owns the call. this room names the bridges vendors actually publish — webex, amazon connect, google ccai through the webex connector, and the microsoft pieces those pages name — and it refuses tenant click-paths, word-error rates, and millisecond budgets this lab did not measure. note verification source note: last-verified was left unmarked until a person checks the cited pages. the citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date. p a virtual agent talks to the caller. agent assist talks to the human who still owns the call. this room names the bridges vendors actually publish — webex, amazon connect, google ccai through the webex connector, and the microsoft pieces those pages name — and it refuses tenant click-paths, word-error rates, and millisecond budgets this lab did not measure. h 01executive summary ul cisco’s webex help page, fetched 2026-10-14, says you can integrate ai agents from webex ai agent studio with voice and digital channels for webex contact center enterprise, unified cce, and contact center express. the page names scripted and autonomous agents as studio tasks. digital channels it names through webex connect are whatsapp, sms, email, facebook messenger, apple messages for business, and live chat. [cite:1] amazon connect’s admin guide describes customer ai agents for self-service on voice and chat, and for real-time assistance to human agents inside the agent workspace: intent, generative responses, links, and actions. amazon q in connect is documented as a generative assistant built on amazon bedrock and as an evolution of amazon connect wisdom. [cite:2] [cite:3] a webex article on integration connectors says webex cce, unified cce, and packaged cce support a google ccai connector. the same article lists other connectors, including google text-to-speech, webex experience management, a custom connector, salesforce, and microsoft teams. a separate ccai article covers virtual agent–voice and agent answers, and it says agent answers is not applicable to the webex contact center solution. [cite:4] [cite:5] microsoft learn pages fetched 2026-10-14 cover copilot in dynamics 365 contact center (embedded and standalone) and dynamics 365 customer service. the help-pane article says representatives can respond to questions, compose emails, and draft chat responses in copilot service workspace. a separate overview describes autonomous agents that converse with customers and hand off to a representative with conversation history. those pages are the article’s procedures, not a walk of the lab tenant. microsoft teams remains a connector the webex article names. the azure certification on the start page is a credential, not a queue. [cite:13] [cite:14] [cite:4] the human still owns an assisted call. the phone system still owns the route. tool execution still belongs to a host, not to the model. mcp revision 2025-11-25, which the versioning page calls current, does not move that execution. [cite:6] note why it matters for the lab engineer contact-center programs buy a virtual agent and an assist pane from different catalogs and then talk about them as one bot. the caller hears one voice. the human sees another. this room is the split: who speaks to the customer, who whispers to the agent, which vendor page names the product, and which numbers you are not allowed to invent. a suggestion that posts a refund without the human is not assist. it is a tool with a side effect, and t4 still has to allow it. h 02architecture p two listeners. the caller hears the virtual agent. the human hears assist. the route stays in the platform. p diagram: seven stages: caller, platform route, virtual agent, knowledge, human desktop, agent assist, and a tool the host must allow ul 1–2 are the caller and the contact-center route. the model is not the acd. 3–4 are a virtual agent and the articles it may quote. abstain if the article is missing. 5–7 are the human, the assist pane, and a tool. assist may suggest. the host executes. p sequence: assist proposes, the human confirms, the host calls the tool once. p diagram: caller, platform, virtual agent, human agent, assist service, and the host that executes a tool p nothing in the picture is a control hub screenshot. vendor guides publish menu paths. those paths describe the vendor’s documentation tenant, not the tenant you have not opened. this room does not reproduce that walk. h 03deep dive p t7-r01 already owns the audio loop: asr or a speech-to-speech session, barge-in, truncation, and the rule that containment is not resolution. this room starts one layer up. some products speak to the customer. some products speak to the employee. some products do both and use different names for each. if you collapse the names, you will scope a pci review and a tool allow-list for the wrong listener. h virtual agent versus agent assist table virtual agent agent assist ['who hears it', 'the caller or the chatter, on a voice or digital channel', 'the human employee, on a desktop'] ['default authority', 'only the tools the host allows for self-service. transfer is a route, not a sentence.', 'none, until the human acts. a suggestion is not a commit.'] ['failure that looks like success', 'high containment, wrong answer, repeat call', 'a pretty card the human never needed, or a card that hides the policy'] ['what t7-r01 still measures', 'endpointing, barge-in, time-to-first-audio on the real edge', 'whether the pane arrived before the human had already spoken. milliseconds stay unmeasured here.'] p amazon’s page is unusually direct about both jobs. connect customer ai agents cover self-service on voice and chat, and they cover real-time assistance to human agents inside the agent workspace. the assistance list on that page includes intent, generative responses, links, and actions. “actions” is the word to circle. an action that moves money is a tool. the workspace showing a button is not the same as the button posting. your host, or the flow you configured, is what posts. [cite:2] note suggest is not seize agent assist that fills the refund field and submits it has become a virtual agent wearing the human’s name. owasp llm06 calls that excessive agency. the pane can draft. the human or a deterministic rule confirms. the idempotency key still lives on your server, because the mcp changelog fetched 2026-10-14 does not add one. [cite:7] [cite:6] h webex ai agent p the help article fetched for this room says ai agents built in webex ai agent studio can be integrated with voice and digital channels for three product lines: webex contact center enterprise, unified contact center enterprise, and contact center express. scripted agents and autonomous agents are both named. scripted means the flow is a designed dialog. autonomous means the article’s own distinction, which you should read on the page before you tell a customer the bot “decides.” this room will not upgrade “autonomous” into “unrestricted tools.” autonomy in a studio is still bounded by the tools and the route the platform will honor. [cite:1] p digital channels named via webex connect on that article are whatsapp, sms, email, facebook messenger, apple messages for business, and live chat. a voice bot and a whatsapp bot can share a knowledge pack and must not share a careless assumption about identity. the person on whatsapp did not pass your voice-biometrics check. the channel is a fact you put in the tool argument. it is not a fact the model may invent. cisco’s configuration article for webex ai agent on cce names cloud connect, control hub, ai agent studio, and webex connect as parts of the integration. that article is a vendor guide. reproducing its clicks as if they had been walked on the lab tenant would be a false log. this room does not reproduce those clicks. [cite:8] h amazon connect and q in connect p amazon q in connect is described, on the cli reference fetched 2026-10-14, as a generative assistant built on amazon bedrock and as an evolution of amazon connect wisdom. the updateassistantaiagent type enum on that reference includes manual_search, answer_recommendation, self_service, email_response, email_overview, email_generative_answer, orchestration, note_taking, and case_summarization. those strings are the api’s names for roles. they are not a promise that every connect instance has every role enabled. read the enum as a menu of intents the api knows, then confirm which association your assistant actually has. [cite:3] p the enablement guide lists a domain or assistant, a kms key, and knowledge-base connectors. connectors named on the page fetched for this room are amazon s3, sharepoint online, salesforce, servicenow, and zendesk. dynamics 365 was not in that list. do not add it as a prebuilt connector because it would be convenient. a case-summarization role that reads a knowledge base still has to obey the pack: if the article does not contain the answer, the assistant should say so, which is the same abstention t3 teaches for embeddings. [cite:9] [cite:10] table q in connect type on the cli page who it is for, in this room’s reading authority ['self_service', 'the caller or chatter', 'only allowed self-service tools. not a second acd.'] ['answer_recommendation, manual_search', 'the human looking for an article', 'show the article. do not invent a policy the article lacks.'] ['email_response, email_overview, email_generative_answer', 'mail, not a voice turn', 'a draft is not a sent message until something sends it.'] ['note_taking, case_summarization', 'the record after or during the contact', 'summaries can hallucinate a promise. prefer tool results over a paragraph.'] ['orchestration', 'a coordinator role the api names', 'not proof of a multi-agent architecture. t4-r09 still wants one host.'] note the enum is not your org chart nine type strings do not mean nine models with nine refund tools. map each enabled type to a tool allow-list. leave the others unassociated. a summarizer that can also call self_service actions has crossed the assist line. h google ccai through the webex connector p this room did not fetch a standalone agent assist page on cloud.google.com. what it fetched is cisco’s connector documentation. the integration-connectors article says webex cce, unified cce, and packaged cce support a google ccai connector, and it lists that connector beside google text-to-speech, webex experience management, a custom connector, salesforce, and microsoft teams. the article includes a control hub path. treat that path as the help article’s path, dated with this fetch, not as a procedure you have executed. [cite:4] p the ccai configuration article discusses virtual agent–voice and agent answers. data centers named on that page are united states, united kingdom, frankfurt, australia, japan, singapore, and canada. the same page says agent answers is not applicable to the webex contact center solution, as distinct from the enterprise, unified cce, and packaged cce products the article is configuring. read that sentence twice before you sell “agent answers on webex contact center.” the product names diverge, and the page is the source. a region list is not a latency sla and not a data-residency legal opinion. [cite:5] h microsoft, only as far as a fetched page p microsoft teams is on the webex connector list above. that is a bridge the cisco article publishes. it is not a specification of how a teams message becomes a contact-center transcript. dynamics 365 is a different product, and it is not one of the amazon connect knowledge connectors named on the enablement page. [cite:4] [cite:9] p the copilot help-pane article applies to dynamics 365 contact center—embedded, dynamics 365 contact center—standalone, and dynamics 365 customer service. it says the help pane lets representatives use copilot to respond to questions, compose emails, and draft chat responses in copilot service workspace. the published enablement steps are support experience, then productivity, then manage on copilot settings, then copilot immersive, copilot side pane, or both. treat that sequence as the article’s path, dated 2026-10-14, not as a menu you have clicked on the lab tenant. queue names on a tenant are not on that page. [cite:13] p the same article says ask a question is available after copilot is enabled and instructions, knowledge sources, and prompts are configured for the customer support agent. using the organization’s knowledge base for ask a question and draft an email is off until you turn it on. the instructions field supports up to 5,000 characters, and prompt-specific instructions support up to 10,000 characters. custom instructions apply only when the organization’s dynamics 365 knowledge base is the selected source. you can add up to five filters per category, and up to five trusted web domains. copilot searches up to two levels down from a configured domain, and the article says external websites are used to draft emails and chat replies only. email sentiments are marked preview on that page. none of those caps is a license count or a pci scope. [cite:13] p the overview page says dynamics 365 customer service and dynamics 365 contact center use ai agents and copilot. autonomous agents can converse with customers, deflect routine issues, collect context, and hand off to a human representative with the full conversation history. the case management agent helps automate the case lifecycle: create, update, resolve, and close. when a representative signs in to a service representative app, copilot opens in the right side panel with the ask a question tab ready. chat with case data is named as a microsoft 365 copilot feature on that page. [cite:14] p the integration article uses the same applies-to line. it says a copilot studio bot is renamed copilot agent, and a human agent is renamed customer service representative. you create the agent in the copilot service admin center and finish it in copilot studio, or you create it in copilot studio and it becomes available in the dynamics 365 contact center admin center. dynamics 365 contact center includes pre-built agents such as the customer assist agent, which handles high-volume voice and digital requests. real-time voice agents in copilot studio are integrated with those pre-built agents. the article says a real-time voice agent supports user interruptions, which it calls barge-in, and it uses the phrase “ultra-low latency” as a description. that phrase is not a millisecond budget. the representative who receives an escalation can see the full transcript. you can add only one agent per workstream, and agents receive conversations only on push-based workstreams. a conversation that is not escalated closes automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity. connecting the agent to the omnichannel instance is a separate procedure this room does not copy click-for-click. the licensing page defines an agent session as a conversation in which the agent is invoked, says two agents in one conversation count as one conversation, and points session entitlements at the dynamics 365 licensing guide. this room does not copy a session count or a price. [cite:15] [cite:16] p the azure ai apps and agents developer associate certification, exam ai-103, is a credential fetched for the start page. passing it does not configure a contact center. [cite:12] table bridge fetched page says this room will not say ['webex ai agent', 'studio agents on voice and digital for three cisco product lines', 'that your control hub matches the article’s clicks'] ['amazon connect', 'self-service and real-time assist. q in connect on bedrock.', 'that every enum value is enabled in your instance'] ['google ccai', 'a connector on webex cce, unified cce, and packaged cce', 'a quota from a cloud.google.com page this pass did not open'] ['dynamics 365 copilot', 'help pane in copilot service workspace; autonomous agents that hand off with history; customer assist agent named for voice and digital', 'a walked tenant queue, a license count, or a claim that dynamics is a connect knowledge connector'] h four calls p call a is self-service. the caller asks for store hours. a virtual agent on connect or a scripted webex ai agent can answer from an article. if the article is missing, the correct behavior is the embeddings guide’s abstention, not a guessed closing time. no human desktop is required. the route back to a queue exists for the case where the caller asks for something the article cannot settle. [cite:10] p call b is assist. a human is already on the phone. answer recommendation or agent answers, on a product where that feature applies, offers a paragraph. the human decides whether to say it. if the pane says “i have issued a credit” and the human reads it aloud, the human has made a promise the tool may not have executed. the repair is to bind spoken promises to tool results, which t7-r01 already requires of the handoff packet. assist that scripts the human into a lie is worse than silence. p call c is a digital channel. the same intent arrives on whatsapp through webex connect. the virtual agent may reuse the knowledge pack. it may not reuse a voice authentication result that never happened. channel is an input to the tool. apple messages for business and facebook messenger are additional names on the same article, not additional identity proofs. [cite:1] p call d is a dynamics contact. the overview says an autonomous agent can collect context and hand off to a representative with the conversation history, and the help-pane article says a representative can ask copilot a question in the side pane. that is a product split you can draw: the agent speaks to the customer, the pane speaks to the representative. it is not a queue name, a dial-plan id, or a session price. teams can still be named because the webex connector article names it, and that name is not a dynamics procedure. the phone system still routes the caller. [cite:14] [cite:13] [cite:4] p across the four calls, do not place a full card number in the assist pane, the summary, or the prompt. owasp llm02 is the name for that disclosure. pci ssc’s page, fetched 2026-10-14, says the standard is for entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder data or sensitive authentication data, and that a qsa assesses. this room does not assign that scope. it also does not publish dial-plan identifiers or an acd reason-code catalog. [cite:7] [cite:17] p knowledge behind any of these products is still retrieval. connect’s listed connectors are s3, sharepoint online, salesforce, servicenow, and zendesk. a vector index you build yourself is t3, including hnsw or ivfflat and a lexical list that is not secretly bm25 inside pgvector. mixing embedding models still breaks neighbors. the contact-center product does not repeal that. if the assist pane quotes a stale article, the defect is freshness, not “the ai.” [cite:9] p observability does not change species because the user is a caller. log the product family, the role (self-service versus assist), the knowledge-base id, the tool name, and the allow or deny. gen_ai.operation.name on the conventions commit this lab pins includes execute_tool and retrieval among its development values. a trace that only says “bot handled it” cannot distinguish call a from a seized assist pane. [cite:11] h what a bridge is, and what a certificate is not p a bridge, in this lab’s ecosystem sense, is a published product boundary: a connector, a studio, an api enum, a channel list. it is evidence you can open. a certificate is a person’s credential. aws certified ai practitioner and aws certified machine learning engineer – associate, the azure ai apps and agents developer associate exam ai-103, and google professional machine learning engineer are named on the start page because their official pages were fetched on 2026-10-14. none of those pages provision a queue. a design review that says “we are covered, someone holds the azure ai engineer cert” is using a retired name and the wrong object. microsoft’s azure ai engineer associate page says that certification and its renewal assessment are retired. the current name this lab will use is the apps and agents developer associate credential. retirement of a cert does not install or remove a contact-center bot. [cite:12] p scripted versus autonomous, on the webex article, is a studio distinction. scripted dialogs are closer to a flow you can draw. autonomous agents are still software someone configured in ai agent studio, integrated into a platform that owns the route. “autonomous” is not a synonym for “the model may call any tool the tenant owns.” map the studio’s tools the same way you map self_service. if the autonomous agent can transfer, the transfer target is a route in the platform, and the identifier of that route is a tenant fact this room does not know. leave the identifier marked. describe the decision: transfer when the article and the allowed tools cannot finish the job, and send the handoff packet. [cite:1] p email roles deserve their own sentence because voice people skip them. email_response, email_overview, and email_generative_answer are on the q in connect enum. an email draft that leaves the building is a send, which is a tool with a side effect, even though nobody barged in. the same allow-list rule applies. a generative answer that quotes a sharepoint article should carry the article id. a generative answer that quotes a refund the knowledge base does not contain is llm09, misinformation, whether or not an attacker was involved. the connector list tells you sharepoint online is a fetched source. it does not tell you the article is current. hash it. [cite:3] [cite:7] p region lists tempt people into latency claims. the ccai article names seven data-center locations. a caller in a country that is not on the list, or a caller whose media hops through a carrier you have not timed, is outside what that list can prove. say “the page lists these regions” and then measure. frankfurt on a page is not 40 milliseconds to your queue. the same discipline applies to connect’s kms key: the enablement guide says to have one. it does not say your key policy matches your recording-retention policy. retention stays an org document. [cite:5] [cite:9] p if you only remember one table from this room, remember the listener. caller, human, or a record written after the fact. self-service, answer recommendation, and case summarization are three listeners wearing api names. give each a pack, a tool list, and a trace field. then the ecosystem map stops being a logo slide and becomes a set of boxes you can incident-review. the logos this room will draw are the ones whose pages were fetched. the logos it will not draw are still available for a later pass, after the fetch, with the mark removed in the same commit as the citation. p voice from t7-r01 still wraps the virtual-agent box. a scripted webex agent on a voice channel is in the asr, model, tts path, or in a speech-to-speech session if that is what you integrated. barge-in still cancels playback and still must truncate unheard audio. assist on the human’s desktop does not play that audio to the caller unless the human reads it. timing the pane with a stopwatch in a lab is not a contact-center sla. this room will not convert the vad guide’s example silence of 500 milliseconds into an assist budget. that figure stays an example in t7-r01. The citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date.</p></aside><p>A virtual agent talks to the caller. Agent assist talks to the human who still owns the call. This room names the bridges vendors actually publish — Webex, Amazon Connect, Google CCAI through the Webex connector, and the Microsoft pieces those pages name — and it refuses tenant click-paths, word-error rates, and millisecond budgets this lab did not measure.</p><h3>01Executive summary</h3><ul><li>Cisco’s Webex help page, fetched 2026-10-14, says you can integrate AI agents from Webex AI Agent Studio with voice and digital channels for Webex Contact Center Enterprise, Unified CCE, and Contact Center Express. The page names scripted and autonomous agents as studio tasks. Digital channels it names through Webex Connect are WhatsApp, SMS, email, Facebook Messenger, Apple Messages for Business, and live chat. [cite:1]</li><li>Amazon Connect’s admin guide describes Customer AI agents for self-service on voice and chat, and for real-time assistance to human agents inside the agent workspace: intent, generative responses, links, and actions. Amazon Q in Connect is documented as a generative assistant built on Amazon Bedrock and as an evolution of Amazon Connect Wisdom. [cite:2] [cite:3]</li><li>A Webex article on integration connectors says Webex CCE, Unified CCE, and Packaged CCE support a Google CCAI connector. The same article lists other connectors, including Google text-to-speech, Webex Experience Management, a custom connector, Salesforce, and Microsoft Teams. A separate CCAI article covers Virtual Agent–voice and Agent Answers, and it says Agent Answers is not applicable to the Webex Contact Center solution. [cite:4] [cite:5]</li><li>Microsoft Learn pages fetched 2026-10-14 cover Copilot in Dynamics 365 Contact Center (embedded and standalone) and Dynamics 365 Customer Service. The help-pane article says representatives can respond to questions, compose emails, and draft chat responses in Copilot Service workspace. A separate overview describes autonomous agents that converse with customers and hand off to a representative with conversation history. Those pages are the article’s procedures, not a walk of the lab tenant. Microsoft Teams remains a connector the Webex article names. The Azure certification on the Start page is a credential, not a queue. [cite:13] [cite:14] [cite:4]</li><li>The human still owns an assisted call. The phone system still owns the route. Tool execution still belongs to a host, not to the model. MCP revision 2025-11-25, which the versioning page calls current, does not move that execution. [cite:6]</li></ul><aside class="callout note"><h3>Why it matters for the lab engineer</h3><p>Contact-center programs buy a virtual agent and an assist pane from different catalogs and then talk about them as one bot. The caller hears one voice. The human sees another. This room is the split: who speaks to the customer, who whispers to the agent, which vendor page names the product, and which numbers you are not allowed to invent. A suggestion that posts a refund without the human is not assist. It is a tool with a side effect, and T4 still has to allow it.</p></aside><h3>02Architecture</h3><p>Two listeners. The caller hears the virtual agent. The human hears assist. The route stays in the platform.</p><p>Diagram: Seven stages: caller, platform route, virtual agent, knowledge, human desktop, agent assist, and a tool the host must allow</p><ul><li>1–2 are the caller and the contact-center route. The model is not the ACD.</li><li>3–4 are a virtual agent and the articles it may quote. Abstain if the article is missing.</li><li>5–7 are the human, the assist pane, and a tool. Assist may suggest. The host executes.</li></ul><p>Sequence: assist proposes, the human confirms, the host calls the tool once.</p><p>Diagram: Caller, platform, virtual agent, human agent, assist service, and the host that executes a tool</p><p>Nothing in the picture is a Control Hub screenshot. Vendor guides publish menu paths. Those paths describe the vendor’s documentation tenant, not the tenant you have not opened. This room does not reproduce that walk.</p><h3>03Deep dive</h3><p>T7-R01 already owns the audio loop: ASR or a speech-to-speech session, barge-in, truncation, and the rule that containment is not resolution. This room starts one layer up. Some products speak to the customer. Some products speak to the employee. Some products do both and use different names for each. If you collapse the names, you will scope a PCI review and a tool allow-list for the wrong listener.</p><h3>Virtual agent versus agent assist</h3><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th></th><th>Virtual agent</th><th>Agent assist</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Who hears it</td><td>The caller or the chatter, on a voice or digital channel</td><td>The human employee, on a desktop</td></tr><tr><td>Default authority</td><td>Only the tools the host allows for self-service. Transfer is a route, not a sentence.</td><td>None, until the human acts. A suggestion is not a commit.</td></tr><tr><td>Failure that looks like success</td><td>High containment, wrong answer, repeat call</td><td>A pretty card the human never needed, or a card that hides the policy</td></tr><tr><td>What T7-R01 still measures</td><td>Endpointing, barge-in, time-to-first-audio on the real edge</td><td>Whether the pane arrived before the human had already spoken. Milliseconds stay unmeasured here.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>Amazon’s page is unusually direct about both jobs. Connect Customer AI agents cover self-service on voice and chat, and they cover real-time assistance to human agents inside the agent workspace. The assistance list on that page includes intent, generative responses, links, and actions. “Actions” is the word to circle. An action that moves money is a tool. The workspace showing a button is not the same as the button posting. Your host, or the flow you configured, is what posts. [cite:2]</p><aside class="callout note"><h3>Suggest is not seize</h3><p>Agent assist that fills the refund field and submits it has become a virtual agent wearing the human’s name. OWASP LLM06 calls that excessive agency. The pane can draft. The human or a deterministic rule confirms. The idempotency key still lives on your server, because the MCP changelog fetched 2026-10-14 does not add one. [cite:7] [cite:6]</p></aside><h3>Webex AI Agent</h3><p>The help article fetched for this room says AI agents built in Webex AI Agent Studio can be integrated with voice and digital channels for three product lines: Webex Contact Center Enterprise, Unified Contact Center Enterprise, and Contact Center Express. Scripted agents and autonomous agents are both named. Scripted means the flow is a designed dialog. Autonomous means the article’s own distinction, which you should read on the page before you tell a customer the bot “decides.” This room will not upgrade “autonomous” into “unrestricted tools.” Autonomy in a studio is still bounded by the tools and the route the platform will honor. [cite:1]</p><p>Digital channels named via Webex Connect on that article are WhatsApp, SMS, email, Facebook Messenger, Apple Messages for Business, and live chat. A voice bot and a WhatsApp bot can share a knowledge pack and must not share a careless assumption about identity. The person on WhatsApp did not pass your voice-biometrics check. The channel is a fact you put in the tool argument. It is not a fact the model may invent. Cisco’s configuration article for Webex AI Agent on CCE names Cloud Connect, Control Hub, AI Agent Studio, and Webex Connect as parts of the integration. That article is a vendor guide. Reproducing its clicks as if they had been walked on the lab tenant would be a false log. This room does not reproduce those clicks. [cite:8]</p><h3>Amazon Connect and Q in Connect</h3><p>Amazon Q in Connect is described, on the CLI reference fetched 2026-10-14, as a generative assistant built on Amazon Bedrock and as an evolution of Amazon Connect Wisdom. The UpdateAssistantAIAgent type enum on that reference includes MANUAL_SEARCH, ANSWER_RECOMMENDATION, SELF_SERVICE, EMAIL_RESPONSE, EMAIL_OVERVIEW, EMAIL_GENERATIVE_ANSWER, ORCHESTRATION, NOTE_TAKING, and CASE_SUMMARIZATION. Those strings are the API’s names for roles. They are not a promise that every Connect instance has every role enabled. Read the enum as a menu of intents the API knows, then confirm which association your assistant actually has. [cite:3]</p><p>The enablement guide lists a domain or assistant, a KMS key, and knowledge-base connectors. Connectors named on the page fetched for this room are Amazon S3, SharePoint Online, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Zendesk. Dynamics 365 was not in that list. Do not add it as a prebuilt connector because it would be convenient. A case-summarization role that reads a knowledge base still has to obey the pack: if the article does not contain the answer, the assistant should say so, which is the same abstention T3 teaches for embeddings. [cite:9] [cite:10]</p><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Q in Connect type on the CLI page</th><th>Who it is for, in this room’s reading</th><th>Authority</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>SELF_SERVICE</td><td>The caller or chatter</td><td>Only allowed self-service tools. Not a second ACD.</td></tr><tr><td>ANSWER_RECOMMENDATION, MANUAL_SEARCH</td><td>The human looking for an article</td><td>Show the article. Do not invent a policy the article lacks.</td></tr><tr><td>EMAIL_RESPONSE, EMAIL_OVERVIEW, EMAIL_GENERATIVE_ANSWER</td><td>Mail, not a voice turn</td><td>A draft is not a sent message until something sends it.</td></tr><tr><td>NOTE_TAKING, CASE_SUMMARIZATION</td><td>The record after or during the contact</td><td>Summaries can hallucinate a promise. Prefer tool results over a paragraph.</td></tr><tr><td>ORCHESTRATION</td><td>A coordinator role the API names</td><td>Not proof of a multi-agent architecture. T4-R09 still wants one host.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><aside class="callout note"><h3>The enum is not your org chart</h3><p>Nine type strings do not mean nine models with nine refund tools. Map each enabled type to a tool allow-list. Leave the others unassociated. A summarizer that can also call SELF_SERVICE actions has crossed the assist line.</p></aside><h3>Google CCAI through the Webex connector</h3><p>This room did not fetch a standalone Agent Assist page on cloud.google.com. What it fetched is Cisco’s connector documentation. The integration-connectors article says Webex CCE, Unified CCE, and Packaged CCE support a Google CCAI connector, and it lists that connector beside Google text-to-speech, Webex Experience Management, a custom connector, Salesforce, and Microsoft Teams. The article includes a Control Hub path. Treat that path as the help article’s path, dated with this fetch, not as a procedure you have executed. [cite:4]</p><p>The CCAI configuration article discusses Virtual Agent–voice and Agent Answers. Data centers named on that page are United States, United Kingdom, Frankfurt, Australia, Japan, Singapore, and Canada. The same page says Agent Answers is not applicable to the Webex Contact Center solution, as distinct from the Enterprise, Unified CCE, and Packaged CCE products the article is configuring. Read that sentence twice before you sell “Agent Answers on Webex Contact Center.” The product names diverge, and the page is the source. A region list is not a latency SLA and not a data-residency legal opinion. [cite:5]</p><h3>Microsoft, only as far as a fetched page</h3><p>Microsoft Teams is on the Webex connector list above. That is a bridge the Cisco article publishes. It is not a specification of how a Teams message becomes a contact-center transcript. Dynamics 365 is a different product, and it is not one of the Amazon Connect knowledge connectors named on the enablement page. [cite:4] [cite:9]</p><p>The Copilot help-pane article applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center—embedded, Dynamics 365 Contact Center—standalone, and Dynamics 365 Customer Service. It says the help pane lets representatives use Copilot to respond to questions, compose emails, and draft chat responses in Copilot Service workspace. The published enablement steps are Support experience, then Productivity, then Manage on Copilot settings, then Copilot immersive, Copilot side pane, or both. lessons.14-p-t7r07:
<article class="lesson" id="14-p-t7r07" data-panel="lesson" data-school="14" data-title="AI in the contact center ecosystem" data-search="14-p-t7r07 ai in the contact center ecosystem a virtual agent talks to the caller. assist talks to the human. a summary is a draft the human still has to read. quality management scores the contact later. a forecast predicts volume and handle time. none of those jobs is the phone system, and none of them is allowed to invent a refund. this room names what webex, google ccai, amazon connect, and dynamics 365 actually print about those jobs, retrieved 2026-10-14. note verification source note: last-verified was left unmarked until a person checks the cited pages. the citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date. p a virtual agent talks to the caller. assist talks to the human. a summary is a draft the human still has to read. quality management scores the contact later. a forecast predicts volume and handle time. none of those jobs is the phone system, and none of them is allowed to invent a refund. this room names what webex, google ccai, amazon connect, and dynamics 365 actually print about those jobs, retrieved 2026-10-14. h 01executive summary ul five jobs sit around one contact. the virtual agent speaks to the customer. agent assist speaks to the human. summarization drafts a recap. quality management scores the interaction after the fact. workforce planning predicts how many people you need. t7-r02 already split the first two. this room is the other three, and the bridges that name them. [cite:1] cisco’s ai-generated summaries article, page date october 06, 2026, retrieved 2026-10-14, says a dropped-call summary can take up to 60 seconds, that virtual-agent handoff summaries cover both escalated and handled calls, and that mid-call summaries are only for direct agent-to-agent consults and transfers. wrap-up is a draft the agent reviews. after wrap-up completes, the article says post-call summaries are stored for 24 hours and can be retrieved with the summaries api. [cite:1] webex ai quality management, article date july 24, 2026, names automated evaluations, sentiment analysis, coaching insights, an agent performance dashboard, and analyzer reports. the article says the feature supports english only for now, and that a paid sku is required. the dashboard’s metrics include average handle time and wrap-up duration. that is a quality view. it is not a schedule. [cite:2] google’s ccai platform agent assist page says assist is in-the-moment help for human agents. generative session summarization appears in the agent adapter at wrap-up. multiple human agents split the session into segments. summary quality is described with three metrics: accuracy, completeness, and adherence. a chat segment is created on transfer to a human or a virtual agent. [cite:3] connect’s administrator guide, retrieved 2026-10-14, calls post-contact summaries a structured recap agents use for after-contact work on voice and email, and that managers can read voice, chat, and email summaries. the same guide’s conversational analytics page is the quality-management description: redact sensitive data, pre-populate evaluation forms, search contacts as far back as two years. forecasting is a separate page: it predicts contact volume and average handle time, short-term for scheduling up to 18 weeks, long-term for capacity up to 64 weeks. intraday forecasts update every 15 minutes and require a minimum of 5000 unique contacts per week, per queue-channel, over the last 4 weeks. [cite:4] [cite:5] [cite:6] dynamics 365’s overview, retrieved the same day, says copilot summarizes chat and transcribed voice conversations. the quality-evaluation article says a supervisor-defined framework scores interactions, generates summaries, and covers cases, closed and active conversations, and emails in preview. the same article says the feature is not for employment decisions, and that customers must notify users and obtain consent where the law requires it. check dynamics’ workforce docs for the product you licensed. scheduling products differ by sku, which is why this room does not treat the quality page as a schedule. [cite:7] [cite:8] note why it matters for the lab engineer the lab engineer is fictional. the design review that fails him is the one that draws one box labeled ai and then asks the box to greet the caller, whisper to the agent, write the note, grade the agent, and staff tuesday. those are five readers of one contact. only the host executes a tool. a summary that says “refund posted” is a sentence until a ledger says so. h 02architecture p five jobs. the platform still routes. the host still executes. quality and forecast read later. p diagram: caller, platform, virtual agent, human with assist, draft summary, quality review, forecast, and host ul the caller hears the virtual agent or the human. assist is on the human’s side of the glass. the summary is a draft. quality scores a finished contact. the forecast does not read the draft. a side effect still waits for the host from t4. a coaching insight is not that host. p after hang-up. the human edits the draft before quality or planning ever sees a number. p diagram: sequence from hang-up through a draft, an edited wrap-up, a later quality score, and a forecast that uses volume p read the pictures as jobs, not as a vendor’s menu. webex, google ccai, connect, and dynamics each publish some of these jobs under their own names. t7-r02 already named who speaks. this room names who writes the note, who scores it, and which page actually predicts staffing. a product that is silent on scheduling stays silent in this room. [cite:6] h 03deep dive p start from the contact, not from the model. a contact is a voice call or a chat that the platform routed. someone spoke to the customer. that someone was a virtual agent, a human, or both in sequence. when the contact ends, other systems want a record: a short recap for the next person, a score for a supervisor, and a count for the person who builds tomorrow’s schedule. those wants are not the same request, and they do not share a permission. h five jobs, five permissions table job who it is for what it may emit what it may not do ['virtual agent', 'the customer', 'speech or chat, and a request the host may refuse', 'become the acd. t7-r01 still owns the route.'] ['agent assist', 'the human on the contact', 'a suggestion, a link, a draft the human can ignore', 'post a side effect while the human is still reading. that is llm06. [cite:9]'] ['summarization', 'the next reader: the same human in wrap-up, or the next agent after a handoff', 'a draft recap of reason, action, and outcome', 'become the system of record. the human edits, or the sentence stays a draft.'] ['quality management', 'a supervisor or quality reviewer, later', 'a score against a form, a sentiment label, a coaching note', 'decide employment, pay, or seniority. dynamics prints that limit. treat it as the careful reading for every vendor. [cite:8]'] ['workforce forecast', 'the person who staffs a queue', 'predicted contact volume and average handle time, on the connect page this room opened', 'read a summary and invent a headcount. the forecast page uses historical metrics. The summary includes the sentence “refund will be posted today,” because the virtual agent was helpful. The tool was never called. The ledger is empty. The human, if they trust the draft, will tell the caller the credit exists. That is LLM09, misinformation, wearing a summary’s voice. The repair is the same as T7-R02: numbers come from a tool result or they do not come. The summary template may have a field for “actions.” The field is empty unless the host committed. [cite:1] [cite:9]</p><p>The human edits the draft, deletes the refund sentence, picks a wrap-up code from the admin list, and completes wrap-up. On Webex, the article says the post-call summary is then stored for 24 hours for the Summaries API. Quality management may later score the contact. If the form asks “did the agent promise money the tool did not post,” the edited note and the tool trace are the evidence. The original draft is the evidence of what the model wanted to say. Keep both if your retention rules allow the draft. Do not keep a card number in either. The Webex article says to verify sensitive information before sharing. Connect’s analytics page says you can redact sensitive data from transcripts and audio. PCI SSC says the standard is a baseline for entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder data, and that assessors perform assessments. This room still does not decide that a recording is in scope. [cite:1] [cite:5] [cite:11]</p><p>The next morning the forecast updates, because short-term forecasts update daily. It does not read the deleted refund sentence. It may notice handle time if the contact’s duration landed in the historical metrics the page says the forecast uses.
