<article class="lesson" id="14-p-t8r03" data-panel="lesson" data-school="14" data-title="Responsible AI and data privacy for voice" data-search="14-p-t8r03 responsible ai and data privacy for voice a voice bot hears account numbers, records a waveform, and writes a transcript into a log that outlives the call. this room separates redaction, consent, and retention, and it refuses to invent a pci scope or a retention period the lab did not read. note verification source note: last-verified was left unmarked until a person checks the cited pages. the citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date. p a voice bot hears account numbers, records a waveform, and writes a transcript into a log that outlives the call. this room separates redaction, consent, and retention, and it refuses to invent a pci scope or a retention period the lab did not read. h 01executive summary ul owasp llm02:2025 is sensitive information disclosure. a card number in a prompt, a transcript, or a trace is that failure. llm07 is system-prompt leakage. the hidden instruction is not a vault for a secret. [cite:1] consent for a side effect is an event the host observed, not a schema field the model sets to true. if the caller speaks over the consent prompt, stop playback and truncate unplayed audio so the model’s history matches what was heard. [cite:2] retention periods, pci scope, and a vendor’s redaction checkbox that this lab did not read stay marked. a conversation that dynamics 365 closes after 30 minutes of inactivity is not a retention policy. [cite:3] the copilot help-pane article says that outside north america, bing-powered web search requires data movement across regions to be enabled in the power platform admin center. that is a data-flow control, not a license to log raw audio. [cite:4] nist measure still means test before deployment. a redaction rule you have not tried against a recording of a fake card number is a slogan. [cite:5] note why it matters for the lab engineer the lab engineer is fictional, not a caller and not a tenant. the mistake the callouts keep using his name to avoid is treating a lab persona as production data. the same mistake, aimed at a real caller, is a transcript that still contains a card number after the “we redact pii” slide. this room is the list of places that number can hide, and the list of numbers this lab will not invent. h 02architecture p audio, transcript, and tool arguments meet a redaction step before any log or model that does not need the raw value. p diagram: caller audio split into a redacted transcript, a consent event, and a retained record p the picture has two outputs on purpose. the model and the tool may need an identifier your directory issued. the log needs a masked string. those are different objects. if you pass the same object to both, you will either break the tool or leak the secret. the consent event sits beside them. it is a record that a specific prompt was played and a specific response was heard, not a boolean inside the model’s json. p barge-in during consent cancels playback and truncates unheard audio before any tool runs. p diagram: caller interrupts a consent prompt, playback stops, and the tool does not run p the sequence is t7-r01’s barge-in rule applied to a privacy decision. `conversation.item.truncate` exists because the server may have sent audio the caller did not hear. a consent clause in that unheard audio is not consent. the tool stays idle. [cite:2] h 03deep dive p voice privacy is harder than chat privacy because the same fact exists three times: in the waveform, in the transcript, and in whatever the model copies into a tool argument or a summary. deleting one copy feels like compliance. the other two remain. this room walks the copies. pci ssc’s standards page, fetched 2026-10-14, says pci dss is a baseline for entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder data or sensitive authentication data, and that qualified security assessors perform assessments. this room does not assign that scope. it does keep a card number out of the model, the log, and the pane. [cite:7] h what counts as sensitive on a call p treat these as sensitive until a written policy says a field is not: payment card numbers, bank numbers, government identifiers, full recordings, authentication secrets, health details a caller volunteers, and the precise location a caller did not need to give. a name plus an account id may be sensitive in combination even when each half looks ordinary. owasp llm02 is the category for putting that material where it does not belong: the prompt, the log, the fine-tune export, the trace vendor. the category does not list your fields for you. you list them, and you mark the list as your policy, not as a finding from a model card. [cite:1] p dtmf digits are not “safer because they were not spoken.” they are often the card number. a media server that logs dtmf for debugging has built a card database. the debug flag is a privacy control. default it off. if you must capture digits to pass them to a payment service, pass them on a channel that service documents, and keep them out of the model context. the model does not need the pan to know that a payment step happened. it needs a result: approved, declined, or failed. the result is not the number. p system prompts are a bad place for secrets and a bad place for a copy of the caller’s data from the previous turn. llm07 says the hidden instruction leaks. anything you put there to “help the model remember the card” will be askable. put the card nowhere near the model. put a token your payment service understands, if the design truly needs a reference, and assume the token can appear in a screenshot. [cite:1] note gotcha summaries feel safe because they are short. a summary that says “caller’s card ending 4242 was charged $80” is still disclosure. the assistant pane in a contact center is a place representatives will read aloud. t7-r02 already says not to put a full card number in the pane, the summary, or the prompt. the last four digits are still more than many policies allow in a log. if your policy does not say, do not guess. mask to a length you were told, or mask the entire field. [cite:1] h redaction is a step, not a slogan p redaction means a deterministic transform before the data reaches a sink that should not see it. the sinks in a voice stack are: the model request, the trace, the call recording archive, the case note, the eval export, and the fine-tune file. each sink can have a different rule. “we redact” without a per-sink rule is how the eval set quietly contains production pans because someone exported “just the failures.” p a regex for sixteen digits is a start and a liar. card numbers contain spaces. people say them in groups. speech-to-text splits them across tokens. a regex on the final transcript misses a number that was correct in the audio and wrong in the words, and it also misses a number that was correct in a tool argument built from dtmf rather than from text. run the scrubber on every representation you store. test it with a fixture that uses a test card number your payment provider publishes for sandboxes, not a real card. store the fixture in the repo only if it is an official test number. do not invent a “looks real” number for the unit test. this room does not print one. p product settings are where teams outsource the scrubber and then stop testing. this room does not name a recording product’s redaction toggle, entity list, or confidence threshold. those differ by vendor and were not on a page fetched for this pass, so the room makes no numeric claim about them. the control it will defend is a fixture: pass a known fake sensitive string through every sink you store and read the log. if the string survives, the toggle is not your control. nist measure is that test, before deployment and again when a default changes. [cite:5] table copy of the fact who wants it what the log should keep ['waveform', 'quality review, dispute, the media server', 'only under a retention decision. default in this lab: do not copy production audio into the repo or the trace.'] ['asr transcript', 'the model, the agent desktop, evals', 'a redacted transcript. raw text is a policy exception, not the default.'] ['dtmf', 'the payment service', 'not the model, not the trace. a result code instead.'] ['tool arguments', 'the host, for debugging', 'ids and amounts you are allowed to store. no pan.'] ['model summary', 'the next representative', 'the handoff packet from tool results, redacted. not a free paraphrase of the card.'] h consent is an event p play a specific sentence. record that it was played to completion or that it was interrupted. record what the caller did next in a way your policy accepts: a spoken yes that your grammar actually matched, a dtmf digit you reserved for yes, or a transfer. do not ask the model to emit `user_confirmed: true` and treat that as the record. t2-r03 already called that field a proposal. a proposal is not evidence. the evidence is the event your media server logged. p barge-in cuts the event short. the realtime conversations guide says you truncate with `conversation.item.truncate` because audio may have been generated past what was played. if the consent clause was in the unplayed tail, the caller did not hear it. do not run the tool. do not let the next turn’s context include the clause as if it had been spoken. t7-r01’s pass rule can say “zero tools if the caller barged in during consent” without knowing the tenant’s menu. that rule is enforceable in the host. this room does not publish a millisecond barge-in target. the control is cancel plus truncate. [cite:2] p consent to be recorded is not consent to train. gdpr article 5(1)(b) is purpose limitation: personal data collected for specified purposes and not further processed in a way incompatible with those purposes. a greeting that says “this call may be recorded” does not state a fine-tune purpose or a trace-export purpose. this room does not claim any script is legally sufficient. that question belongs to counsel. the engineering habit is to refuse the export when the event is missing. [cite:8] note recording is not the same as a transcript a caller can consent to a recording the quality team hears and still not have consented to a full transcript in an llm log that a hundred engineers can search. split the purposes. the audio archive and the model log are different systems with different audiences. access to one is not access to the other. h retention is a decision you write down p gdpr article 5(1)(e) is storage limitation: identifiable personal data kept no longer than necessary for the purposes. it is not a universal day count. article 5(1)(c) is data minimisation: adequate, relevant, and limited to what the purpose needs. on openai’s data-controls page fetched 2026-10-14, abuse-monitoring logs that can contain api prompts and responses are retained for up to 30 days by default, unless the law or harm prevention requires longer. zero data retention is an approval, not the default. the same page lists chat completions, responses, and the realtime api as not used for training, with that 30-day abuse-monitoring window, and lists realtime application state as none. the enterprise privacy page, updated 8 january 2026, says the same “up to 30 days” for api inputs and outputs, and that deleted chatgpt enterprise conversations are removed within 30 days unless the law requires longer. a local archive can be shorter. this room does not invent your archive’s integer. the decision you write down still has a purpose, a sink, a duration you chose, an owner, and a deletion job you have run in a test. [cite:8] [cite:9] [cite:10] p dynamics 365’s integration article says a conversation that is not escalated closes automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity. that is a session-close behavior on that page, fetched 2026-10-14. it does not say the transcript is deleted. it does not say the recording is deleted. closing a conversation and deleting the data are different operations. do not put 30 in the retention column of your worksheet. put it in the product-behavior column, with the citation, and leave retention blank until the policy speaks. [cite:3] p the same article’s privacy notice says data might be transmitted to external systems and might flow outside the organization’s compliance boundary, including when the organization is in a government cloud, because messages are shared with the agent. that is a reason to know which tools the agent can call. it is not a reason to panic-copy a prohibition this room did not read. read the notice, list the external systems you actually enabled, and treat each one as a sink in the table above. [cite:3] p the copilot help-pane article adds a narrower data-movement fact. if you are not in the north america region and you want web search powered by bing, you must enable data movement across regions and bing search in the power platform admin center. turning that on so a representative’s draft email can use the web is a cross-region flow. it is optional in the sense that the article ties it to the bing feature. do not enable it because a setup guide’s first checkbox looked mandatory. do not describe it as the retention period. [cite:4] h traces and evals are sinks p t5-r06 says to store raw caller text only under a retention decision, and to default the lab to not storing it. this room is that decision’s privacy half. a trace needs the model id, the operation name, the tool name, the allow or deny, and token counts. it does not need the pan to explain a slow hop. redact arguments before they are attached to the span. if the tracing vendor samples bodies, assume a sample will be read by someone who is not on the incident. sampling is not a security boundary. p eval exports are how sensitive data becomes a permanent fixture. a “failure” case that includes the real transcript will be copied into git, into a slide, and into a fine-tune. build golden cases from synthetic data. if you must use a production snippet, run the same scrubber and have a person check it. llm04, data poisoning, is the adjacent risk: a scrubbed file can still contain an instruction. privacy and poisoning share a review step. they are not the same control. [cite:1] p fine-tune files are worse than eval files because the model can memorize them. t6’s gate already says the train file must not contain the held-out questions. add: the train file must not contain a pan, a recording, or a secret from the system prompt. a weight update is not a deletion mechanism. if a secret went into a training run, rotating the secret is necessary and may not be sufficient. say that plainly to the interviewer. do not claim you can “unlearn” a card number because a paper used that verb. table decision this room’s answer still marked ['may the model see a pan?', 'no. pass a payment result, not the number.', 'the payment service’s own api, which you must read.'] ['may the trace contain raw audio?', 'not in this lab’s repo.', 'if the audio went to the openai api, the fetched default abuse-monitoring window is up to 30 days. a shorter local rule is yours to write. [cite:7]'] h access, deletion, and the person who can actually delete p a privacy request fails when the data lives in five sinks and only one of them has a delete button. list the sinks before you promise a date. the california attorney general’s ccpa page, fetched 2026-10-14, says a person may request deletion of personal information a business collected from them, with exceptions, including when the law requires the business to keep it. the same page says the business must respond within 45 calendar days and may extend by another 45 days, 90 in total, if it notifies the person. that is a response window, not a retention period. for this stack the sink list is at least: media recording, transcript store, case record, trace backend, model-provider logs, and any eval or fine-tune copy. openai’s fetched default for api abuse monitoring is up to 30 days, and fine-tuning files on the enterprise page are retained until the customer deletes them. do not write “zero retention” on a slide unless the account is approved for that control. [cite:9] [cite:10] [cite:11] p access control is the other half of llm02. a trace ui that every engineer can search is a broad audience for a narrow purpose. role-gate the raw view. give on-call the redacted view by default. break-glass access should write its own audit event. if your tool cannot do that, do not store the raw view there. nist govern is the ownership: someone can say who is allowed to listen. manage is what you do when the wrong person did. [cite:5] p cross-region flows need the same list. the bing data-movement checkbox is one flow, and only when that feature is on. a trace vendor’s region is another. a model endpoint’s region is a third. write them down as architecture, not as a vibe that “the cloud is secure.” the dynamics privacy notice is explicit that data can leave a compliance boundary because you integrated an agent. your design review should be able to point at each hop. [cite:3] [cite:4] h what the representative is allowed to see p agent assist shows text to a human who will say it out loud. that human is an audience. a suggestion that includes a card number, a full social identifier, or a diagnosis the caller whispered to the bot is a disclosure with a speaker. the handoff packet from t7 is intent, checks already done, promises already kept by tools, and a transcript span. the span should already be redacted. if the desktop product cannot redact, redact before you hand it the string. do not rely on the representative to notice. p autonomous agents that hand off with full conversation history, which the dynamics overview describes, will hand off whatever history you stored. “full” is a product behavior. it is also a privacy requirement to define full as “full minus the fields you scrubbed,” or you will forward dtmf. configure the history from the redacted transcript. say so in the design. the article’s phrase is not permission to forward secrets. [cite:6] p masking and hashing are different tools and people mix the names. masking replaces digits with a symbol so a human can see that a number was present and cannot read it. hashing is for a join key you might need later, and a hash of a card number is still sensitive if the space of card numbers is small enough to guess. do not hash a pan and call the hash anonymous. do not keep the raw value “only in the hash lookup table” on the same disk as the hash and call that separation. if you do not need to join, do not keep a derivative. the eval case can say “a payment was attempted” without any derivative at all. that sentence is enough for a trajectory test of “zero tools during interrupted consent.” it does not need the secret to be a realistic test, and a realistic test is how secrets enter git. p access logs are part of the sensitive story even when the audio is gone. a line that says which engineer played which recording is itself a record you retain under the same decision, or you cannot investigate the investigation. write that log without the audio payload. nist manage includes communicate: if the wrong person played a recording, the people affected are not soothed by a deleted file you cannot prove was the only copy. the proof is the sink list plus the deletion job’s output. until the job exists, say so. a roadmap item is not a control. This room separates redaction, consent, and retention, and it refuses to invent a PCI scope or a retention period the lab did not read.</p><h3>01Executive summary</h3><ul><li>OWASP LLM02:2025 is sensitive information disclosure. A card number in a prompt, a transcript, or a trace is that failure. LLM07 is system-prompt leakage. The hidden instruction is not a vault for a secret. [cite:1]</li><li>Consent for a side effect is an event the host observed, not a schema field the model sets to true. If the caller speaks over the consent prompt, stop playback and truncate unplayed audio so the model’s history matches what was heard. [cite:2]</li><li>Retention periods, PCI scope, and a vendor’s redaction checkbox that this lab did not read stay marked. A conversation that Dynamics 365 closes after 30 minutes of inactivity is not a retention policy. [cite:3]</li><li>The Copilot help-pane article says that outside North America, Bing-powered web search requires data movement across regions to be enabled in the Power Platform admin center. That is a data-flow control, not a license to log raw audio. [cite:4]</li><li>NIST Measure still means test before deployment. A redaction rule you have not tried against a recording of a fake card number is a slogan. [cite:5]</li></ul><aside class="callout note"><h3>Why it matters for the lab engineer</h3><p>the lab engineer is fictional, not a caller and not a tenant. The mistake the callouts keep using his name to avoid is treating a lab persona as production data. The same mistake, aimed at a real caller, is a transcript that still contains a card number after the “we redact PII” slide. This room is the list of places that number can hide, and the list of numbers this lab will not invent.</p></aside><h3>02Architecture</h3><p>Audio, transcript, and tool arguments meet a redaction step before any log or model that does not need the raw value.</p><p>Diagram: Caller audio split into a redacted transcript, a consent event, and a retained record</p><p>The picture has two outputs on purpose. The model and the tool may need an identifier your directory issued. The log needs a masked string. Those are different objects. If you pass the same object to both, you will either break the tool or leak the secret. The consent event sits beside them. It is a record that a specific prompt was played and a specific response was heard, not a boolean inside the model’s JSON.</p><p>Barge-in during consent cancels playback and truncates unheard audio before any tool runs.</p><p>Diagram: Caller interrupts a consent prompt, playback stops, and the tool does not run</p><p>The sequence is T7-R01’s barge-in rule applied to a privacy decision. <code>conversation.item.truncate</code> exists because the server may have sent audio the caller did not hear. A consent clause in that unheard audio is not consent. The tool stays idle. [cite:2]</p><h3>03Deep dive</h3><p>Voice privacy is harder than chat privacy because the same fact exists three times: in the waveform, in the transcript, and in whatever the model copies into a tool argument or a summary. Deleting one copy feels like compliance. The other two remain. This room walks the copies. PCI SSC’s standards page, fetched 2026-10-14, says PCI DSS is a baseline for entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder data or sensitive authentication data, and that Qualified Security Assessors perform assessments. This room does not assign that scope. It does keep a card number out of the model, the log, and the pane. [cite:7]</p><h3>What counts as sensitive on a call</h3><p>Treat these as sensitive until a written policy says a field is not: payment card numbers, bank numbers, government identifiers, full recordings, authentication secrets, health details a caller volunteers, and the precise location a caller did not need to give. A name plus an account id may be sensitive in combination even when each half looks ordinary. OWASP LLM02 is the category for putting that material where it does not belong: the prompt, the log, the fine-tune export, the trace vendor. The category does not list your fields for you. You list them, and you mark the list as your policy, not as a finding from a model card. [cite:1]</p><p>DTMF digits are not “safer because they were not spoken.” They are often the card number. A media server that logs DTMF for debugging has built a card database. The debug flag is a privacy control. Default it off. If you must capture digits to pass them to a payment service, pass them on a channel that service documents, and keep them out of the model context. The model does not need the PAN to know that a payment step happened. It needs a result: approved, declined, or failed. The result is not the number.</p><p>System prompts are a bad place for secrets and a bad place for a copy of the caller’s data from the previous turn. LLM07 says the hidden instruction leaks. Anything you put there to “help the model remember the card” will be askable. Put the card nowhere near the model. Put a token your payment service understands, if the design truly needs a reference, and assume the token can appear in a screenshot. [cite:1]</p><aside class="callout note"><h3>Gotcha</h3><p>Summaries feel safe because they are short. A summary that says “caller’s card ending 4242 was charged $80” is still disclosure. The assistant pane in a contact center is a place representatives will read aloud. T7-R02 already says not to put a full card number in the pane, the summary, or the prompt. The last four digits are still more than many policies allow in a log. If your policy does not say, do not guess. Mask to a length you were told, or mask the entire field. [cite:1]</p></aside><h3>Redaction is a step, not a slogan</h3><p>Redaction means a deterministic transform before the data reaches a sink that should not see it. The sinks in a voice stack are: the model request, the trace, the call recording archive, the case note, the eval export, and the fine-tune file. Each sink can have a different rule. “We redact” without a per-sink rule is how the eval set quietly contains production PANs because someone exported “just the failures.”</p><p>A regex for sixteen digits is a start and a liar. Card numbers contain spaces. People say them in groups. Speech-to-text splits them across tokens. A regex on the final transcript misses a number that was correct in the audio and wrong in the words, and it also misses a number that was correct in a tool argument built from DTMF rather than from text. Run the scrubber on every representation you store. Test it with a fixture that uses a test card number your payment provider publishes for sandboxes, not a real card. Store the fixture in the repo only if it is an official test number. Do not invent a “looks real” number for the unit test. This room does not print one.</p><p>Product settings are where teams outsource the scrubber and then stop testing. This room does not name a recording product’s redaction toggle, entity list, or confidence threshold. Those differ by vendor and were not on a page fetched for this pass, so the room makes no numeric claim about them. The control it will defend is a fixture: pass a known fake sensitive string through every sink you store and read the log. If the string survives, the toggle is not your control. NIST Measure is that test, before deployment and again when a default changes. Default in this lab: do not copy production audio into the repo or the trace.</td></tr><tr><td>ASR transcript</td><td>The model, the agent desktop, evals</td><td>A redacted transcript. Raw text is a policy exception, not the default.</td></tr><tr><td>DTMF</td><td>The payment service</td><td>Not the model, not the trace. A result code instead.</td></tr><tr><td>Tool arguments</td><td>The host, for debugging</td><td>Ids and amounts you are allowed to store. No PAN.</td></tr><tr><td>Model summary</td><td>The next representative</td><td>The handoff packet from tool results, redacted. Not a free paraphrase of the card.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><h3>Consent is an event</h3><p>Play a specific sentence. Record that it was played to completion or that it was interrupted. Record what the caller did next in a way your policy accepts: a spoken yes that your grammar actually matched, a DTMF digit you reserved for yes, or a transfer. Do not ask the model to emit <code>user_confirmed: true</code> and treat that as the record. T2-R03 already called that field a proposal. A proposal is not evidence. The evidence is the event your media server logged.</p><p>Barge-in cuts the event short. The Realtime conversations guide says you truncate with <code>conversation.item.truncate</code> because audio may have been generated past what was played. If the consent clause was in the unplayed tail, the caller did not hear it. Do not run the tool. Do not let the next turn’s context include the clause as if it had been spoken. T7-R01’s pass rule can say “zero tools if the caller barged in during consent” without knowing the tenant’s menu. That rule is enforceable in the host. This room does not publish a millisecond barge-in target. The control is cancel plus truncate. [cite:2]</p><p>Consent to be recorded is not consent to train. GDPR Article 5(1)(b) is purpose limitation: personal data collected for specified purposes and not further processed in a way incompatible with those purposes. A greeting that says “this call may be recorded” does not state a fine-tune purpose or a trace-export purpose. This room does not claim any script is legally sufficient. That question belongs to counsel. The engineering habit is to refuse the export when the event is missing. [cite:8]</p><aside class="callout note"><h3>Recording is not the same as a transcript</h3><p>A caller can consent to a recording the quality team hears and still not have consented to a full transcript in an LLM log that a hundred engineers can search. Split the purposes. The audio archive and the model log are different systems with different audiences. Access to one is not access to the other.</p></aside><h3>Retention is a decision you write down</h3><p>GDPR Article 5(1)(e) is storage limitation: identifiable personal data kept no longer than necessary for the purposes. It is not a universal day count. Article 5(1)(c) is data minimisation: adequate, relevant, and limited to what the purpose needs. On OpenAI’s data-controls page fetched 2026-10-14, abuse-monitoring logs that can contain API prompts and responses are retained for up to 30 days by default, unless the law or harm prevention requires longer. Zero Data Retention is an approval, not the default. The same page lists Chat Completions, Responses, and the Realtime API as not used for training, with that 30-day abuse-monitoring window, and lists Realtime application state as none. The enterprise privacy page, updated 8 January 2026, says the same “up to 30 days” for API inputs and outputs, and that deleted ChatGPT Enterprise conversations are removed within 30 days unless the law requires longer. A local archive can be shorter. This room does not invent your archive’s integer. The decision you write down still has a purpose, a sink, a duration you chose, an owner, and a deletion job you have run in a test. [cite:8] [cite:9] [cite:10]</p><p>Dynamics 365’s integration article says a conversation that is not escalated closes automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity. That is a session-close behavior on that page, fetched 2026-10-14. It does not say the transcript is deleted. It does not say the recording is deleted. Closing a conversation and deleting the data are different operations. Do not put 30 in the retention column of your worksheet. Put it in the product-behavior column, with the citation, and leave retention blank until the policy speaks. [cite:3]</p><p>The same article’s privacy notice says data might be transmitted to external systems and might flow outside the organization’s compliance boundary, including when the organization is in a government cloud, because messages are shared with the agent. That is a reason to know which tools the agent can call. It is not a reason to panic-copy a prohibition this room did not read. Read the notice, list the external systems you actually enabled, and treat each one as a sink in the table above. [cite:3]</p><p>The Copilot help-pane article adds a narrower data-movement fact. If you are not in the North America region and you want web search powered by Bing, you must enable data movement across regions and Bing search in the Power Platform admin center. Turning that on so a representative’s draft email can use the web is a cross-region flow. It is optional in the sense that the article ties it to the Bing feature. Do not enable it because a setup guide’s first checkbox looked mandatory. Do not describe it as the retention period. [cite:4]</p><h3>Traces and evals are sinks</h3><p>T5-R06 says to store raw caller text only under a retention decision, and to default the lab to not storing it. This room is that decision’s privacy half. A trace needs the model id, the operation name, the tool name, the allow or deny, and token counts. It does not need the PAN to explain a slow hop. Redact arguments before they are attached to the span. If the tracing vendor samples bodies, assume a sample will be read by someone who is not on the incident. Sampling is not a security boundary.</p><p>Eval exports are how sensitive data becomes a permanent fixture. A “failure” case that includes the real transcript will be copied into git, into a slide, and into a fine-tune. Build golden cases from synthetic data. If you must use a production snippet, run the same scrubber and have a person check it. LLM04, data poisoning, is the adjacent risk: a scrubbed file can still contain an instruction. Privacy and poisoning share a review step. They are not the same control. [cite:1]</p><p>Fine-tune files are worse than eval files because the model can memorize them. T6’s gate already says the train file must not contain the held-out questions. Add: the train file must not contain a PAN, a recording, or a secret from the system prompt. A weight update is not a deletion mechanism. If a secret went into a training run, rotating the secret is necessary and may not be sufficient. Say that plainly to the interviewer. Do not claim you can “unlearn” a card number because a paper used that verb.</p><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Decision</th><th>This room’s answer</th><th>Still marked</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>May the model see a PAN?</td><td>No. Pass a payment result, not the number.</td><td>The payment service’s own API, which you must read.</td></tr><tr><td>May the trace contain raw audio?</td><td>Not in this lab’s repo.</td><td>If the audio went to the OpenAI API, the fetched default abuse-monitoring window is up to 30 days. A shorter local rule is yours to write. [cite:9]</td></tr><tr><td>Does 30 minutes of inactivity delete data?</td><td>No. The fetched article says the conversation closes.</td><td>Whatever your archive actually does.</td></tr><tr><td>Is barge-in during consent a tool call?</td><td>No. Zero tools. Truncate unheard audio.</td><td>No millisecond target is published in this room.</td></tr><tr><td>Is PCI scope decided here?</td><td>No.</td><td>PCI SSC describes who the standard is for. A QSA assesses. This room assigns neither in nor out. [cite:7]</td></tr></tbody></table></div><h3>Access, deletion, and the person who can actually delete</h3><p>A privacy request fails when the data lives in five sinks and only one of them has a delete button. List the sinks before you promise a date. The California Attorney General’s CCPA page, fetched 2026-10-14, says a person may request deletion of personal information a business collected from them, with exceptions, including when the law requires the business to keep it. The same page says the business must respond within 45 calendar days and may extend by another 45 days, 90 in total, if it notifies the person. That is a response window, not a retention period. For this stack the sink list is at least: media recording, transcript store, case record, trace backend, model-provider logs, and any eval or fine-tune copy. OpenAI’s fetched default for API abuse monitoring is up to 30 days, and fine-tuning files on the enterprise page are retained until the customer deletes them. Do not write “zero retention” on a slide unless the account is approved for that control. [cite:9] [cite:10] [cite:11]</p><p>Access control is the other half of LLM02. A trace UI that every engineer can search is a broad audience for a narrow purpose. Role-gate the raw view. Give on-call the redacted view by default. Break-glass access should write its own audit event. If your tool cannot do that, do not store the raw view there. NIST Govern is the ownership: someone can say who is allowed to listen. Manage is what you do when the wrong person did. [cite:5]</p><p>Cross-region flows need the same list. The Bing data-movement checkbox is one flow, and only when that feature is on. A trace vendor’s region is another. A model endpoint’s region is a third. Write them down as architecture, not as a vibe that “the cloud is secure.” The Dynamics privacy notice is explicit that data can leave a compliance boundary because you integrated an agent. Your design review should be able to point at each hop. [cite:3] [cite:4]</p><h3>What the representative is allowed to see</h3><p>Agent assist shows text to a human who will say it out loud. That human is an audience. A suggestion that includes a card number, a full social identifier, or a diagnosis the caller whispered to the bot is a disclosure with a speaker. The handoff packet from T7 is intent, checks already done, promises already kept by tools, and a transcript span. The span should already be redacted. If the desktop product cannot redact, redact before you hand it the string. Do not rely on the representative to notice.</p><p>Autonomous agents that hand off with full conversation history, which the Dynamics overview describes, will hand off whatever history you stored. “Full” is a product behavior. It is also a privacy requirement to define full as “full minus the fields you scrubbed,” or you will forward DTMF. Configure the history from the redacted transcript. Say so in the design. The article’s phrase is not permission to forward secrets. [cite:6]</p><p>Masking and hashing are different tools and people mix the names. Masking replaces digits with a symbol so a human can see that a number was present and cannot read it. Hashing is for a join key you might need later, and a hash of a card number is still sensitive if the space of card numbers is small enough to guess. Do not hash a PAN and call the hash anonymous. Do not keep the raw value “only in the hash lookup table” on the same disk as the hash and call that separation. If you do not need to join, do not keep a derivative. The eval case can say “a payment was attempted” without any derivative at all. That sentence is enough for a trajectory test of “zero tools during interrupted consent.” It does not need the secret to be a realistic test, and a realistic test is how secrets enter git.</p><p>Access logs are part of the sensitive story even when the audio is gone. A line that says which engineer played which recording is itself a record you retain under the same decision, or you cannot investigate the investigation. Write that log without the audio payload. NIST Manage includes communicate: if the wrong person played a recording, the people affected are not soothed by a deleted file you cannot prove was the only copy. The proof is the sink list plus the deletion job’s output. Until the job exists, say so. A roadmap item is not a control. Truncate the unheard audio in the model session if you are on the API that documents truncate. Mark the consent event as interrupted, not as granted. Do not open the payment tool. The digits already received, if any, go to a buffer that is not the model context. If the caller abandons, wipe the buffer in your code. This room does not claim that a framework wipes it for you.</p><h3>What the log contains</h3><p>An operation name, a deny or a “not attempted,” the model id, and a note that consent was interrupted. It does not contain the digits. It does not contain the unplayed consent paragraph as if the caller heard it. A reviewer can reconstruct the decision without reconstructing the card.</p><h3>What a bad summary would do</h3><p>The model, if you asked it to summarize anyway, might write “customer began reading a Visa ending in …”. That string is a leak even when the digits are partial. Do not ask for that summary on this path. The packet says: payment not attempted, consent interrupted. Template the sentence.</p><ol><li>Classify the field before the call, not during the incident.</li><li>Play consent as a known prompt with an event.</li><li>On barge-in, stop, truncate, zero tools.</li><li>Redact every sink you listed, including the one you added last week.</li><li>Retain only what a written decision names. Leave the integer marked until you have it.</li><li>Test with a fake sensitive string and read the log.</li></ol><h3>05Implementation</h3><ol><li>Write the sink list: recording, transcript, case, trace, provider logs, eval, fine-tune. [cite:7] [cite:9] [cite:11]</p><h3>L4 · What does Measure require of a redaction claim?</h3><p>A test before deployment, and again when the default changes. Pass a known sensitive fixture through the path and read the log. [cite:5]</p><h3>L5 · What would you change in the desktop, and what stops you?</h3><p>I would show a templated packet from redacted tool results and hide raw arguments. What stops a looser pane is a representative who will read the screen aloud. A full history handoff, as the Dynamics overview describes it, must be a history you already scrubbed. [cite:6]</p><h3>Leaf · May this lab store production audio?</h3><p>Not in this lab’s repo. If you sent it to the OpenAI API, the fetched default abuse-monitoring window is up to 30 days, and Zero Data Retention is an approval. [cite:9]</p><h3>Leaf · What do you do if a PAN reached a fine-tune file?</h3><p>Stop the job. Do not describe the weights as a delete button. T6’s gate should have rejected the file.</p><h3>Leaf · Who is the lab engineer?</h3><p>A fictional lab engineer used in callouts. Not a caller, not a tenant, and not a reason to log a real person’s name.</p><h3>09Lab</h3><p>Paper and a fake string you invented that is obviously not a real card, such as the token <code>TEST-SECRET-VALUE</code>. No customer audio. No real payment numbers.</p><ol><li>List seven sinks. Mark which ones exist in your design.</li><li>Write the three consent states and the tool’s required state.</li><li>Write the barge-in steps: stop, truncate, zero tools. [cite:2]</li><li>Write one sentence that uses 30 minutes correctly and one that would be a mistake. [cite:3]</li><li>Leave PCI, retention days, and redaction thresholds blank. Write TODO in those cells.</li><li>Describe the test you would run before believing a redaction toggle. [cite:5]</li></ol><h3>10Quiz</h3><p>Multiple choice</p><h3>Q1. LLM02 names:</h3><ol><li>Sensitive information disclosure.</li><li>A retention period of 30 days.</li><li>A PCI certification.</li><li>A vector index.</li></ol><h3>Reveal</h3><p>A. [cite:1]</p><p>Multiple choice</p><h3>Q2. A schema field user_confirmed true means:</h3><ol><li>The host observed a completed consent prompt.</li><li>The model proposed a boolean. It is not the consent event.</li><li>PCI scope is settled.</li><li>The recording may be used for training.</li></ol><h3>Reveal</h3><p>B.</p><p>Multiple choice</p><h3>Q3. conversation.item.truncate exists because:</h3><ol><li>The server may have emitted audio the caller has not heard.</li><li>JSON schemas require it.</li><li>Retention expired.</li><li>Bing search is on.</li></ol><h3>Reveal</h3><p>A. Unheard consent is not consent. [cite:2]</p><p>Multiple choice</p><h3>Q4. Thirty minutes in the Dynamics integration article is:</h3><ol><li>The time after which an unescalated conversation closes.</li><li>A legal retention period for recordings.</li><li>A PCI safe harbor.</li><li>The barge-in SLO.</li></ol><h3>Reveal</h3><p>A. Close is not deletion. [cite:3]</p><p>Multiple choice</p><h3>Q5. Data movement across regions, on the help-pane article, is required when:</h3><ol><li>You always log audio.</li><li>You are outside North America and want Bing-powered web search.</li><li>You use a JSON schema.</li><li>You pin an OpenTelemetry commit.</li></ol><h3>Reveal</h3><p>B. [cite:4]</p><p>Scenario</p><h3>Q6. The caller says “wait” during the consent sentence and the tool still charges the card. What failed?</h3><ol><li>The host treated an interrupted prompt as consent.</li><li>The embedding width.</li><li>RRF’s constant.</li><li>The 2017 BLEU score.</li></ol><h3>Reveal</h3><p>A. Zero tools on that path. [cite:2]</p><p>Scenario</p><h3>Q7. A slide says the bot is PCI compliant. No QSA assessment is in the worksheet. You:</h3><ol><li>Leave the claim. The slide is shorter.</li><li>Remove the claim. PCI SSC describes who the standard is for. A QSA assesses. This room does not assign scope.</li><li>Add a sixteen-digit example to the repo so people can see.</li><li>Put the PAN in the system prompt so the model can mask it.</li></ol><h3>Reveal</h3><p>B. [cite:7]</p><p>Scenario</p><h3>Q8. Full conversation history is handed to a representative. The history includes DTMF. The repair is:</h3><ol><li>Hand off the redacted transcript, not the digit buffer.</li><li>Ask the model to summarize the digits more politely.</li><li>Cite 30 minutes and assume deletion.</li><li>Enable Bing search.</li></ol><h3>Reveal</h3><p>A. “Full history” is whatever you stored. [cite:6]</p><p>Short answer</p><h3>Q9. Why is a regex on the final transcript not enough?</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>The number may live in the audio, in DTMF, or in a tool argument the transcript regex never saw. Scrub every sink you store.</p><p>Short answer</p><h3>Q10. What does Measure add to a redaction toggle?</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>A test before deployment and again in operation. The toggle’s marketing sentence is not the test. [cite:5]</p><p>Short answer</p><h3>Q11. Name two things this room will not invent.</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>A PCI scope and a retention period. Also a redaction-product threshold that was not fetched.</p><p>Apply</p><h3>Q12. A fine-tune export contains a PAN. What is the weights file not?</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>A deletion mechanism. Stop the job. Scrub the file. Do not claim the model forgot the number because training stopped.</p><h3>11Audio</h3><p>Slots are silent until the lab engineer records them. The file is local silence so the page plays without a network. the lab engineer is fictional, not a caller whose audio you may store.</p><p>Concept · 3 min · Studio fills concept.mp3</p><h3>Transcript prompt</h3><p>Name the copies of a secret. Separate close from delete. Say which numbers stay marked.</p><p>Walk-through · 5 min · Studio fills walkthrough.mp3</p><h3>Transcript prompt</h3><p>Walk barge-in during consent. Zero tools. No digits in the log.</p><p>Oral drill · 2 min · Studio fills oral-drill.mp3</p><h3>Transcript prompt</h3><p>Ask for LLM02, the Bing data-movement prerequisite, and why a summary can still leak.</p><h3>13Citations</h3><ol><li>OWASP, “LLM Top 10,” 2025, including LLM02, LLM04, and LLM07. — industry standard — fetched 2026-10-14 — https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/</li><li>OpenAI, “Realtime conversations,” interruption and truncation, including conversation.item.truncate. — vendor docs — fetched 2026-10-14 — https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-conversations</li><li>Microsoft, “Integrate a Copilot agent in Dynamics 365 Contact Center,” including the 30-minute inactivity close and the privacy notice. — vendor docs — fetched 2026-10-14 — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/configure-bot-virtual-agent</li><li>Microsoft, “Enable features in Copilot pane,” including Bing search and data movement across regions. — vendor docs — fetched 2026-10-14 — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/contact-center/administer/copilot-enable-help-pane</li><li>NIST, AI RMF 1.0. Name an owner per sink.</td></tr><tr><td>Fine-tuning (T6)</td><td>The train file is a permanent copy.</td><td>A way to delete a number already in the weights.</td><td>Keep production secrets out of the export.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>Privacy work fails at the boundary between teams. The media team owns the waveform. The model team owns the prompt. The platform team owns the trace. Each assumes another team redacted. The worksheet is the object they review together. When a new sister technology arrives, a vector store of call summaries for example, it is a new sink before it is a feature. Embeddings of raw transcripts are still the transcripts, in a form you cannot grep and cannot casually “just search.” T3’s index is not a shredder. If you embed, embed the redacted text, and keep the same retention decision on the index that you keep on the source. A vector database does not outlive its policy just because the policy was written for files.</p><h3>Interview answers</h3><p>The spoken answers for this room are in Interview practice. lessons.14-p-t8r08:
<article class="lesson" id="14-p-t8r08" data-panel="lesson" data-school="14" data-title="Build a RAG voice agent for a contact center" data-search="14-p-t8r08 build a rag voice agent for a contact center one design, end to end: a caller asks a question, a retriever packs evidence, a model may request a tool, and a human queue still exists. this room is the architecture, the eval plan, and the rollout. it does not invent a dial plan, a word-error rate, or a millisecond promise. note verification source note: last-verified was left unmarked until a person checks the cited pages. the citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date. p one design, end to end: a caller asks a question, a retriever packs evidence, a model may request a tool, and a human queue still exists. this room is the architecture, the eval plan, and the rollout. it does not invent a dial plan, a word-error rate, or a millisecond promise. h 01executive summary ul the architecture is a cascade you can point at: media edge, retrieval, a model that may request a tool, a host that executes, and an acd that still owns the route. speech-to-speech collapses some hops. it does not delete the queue. [cite:1] grounding follows the embeddings guide: if the packed articles do not contain the answer, say you do not know. one embedding model per index. hybrid search is t3-r04, not a feeling that “vectors are enough.” [cite:2] the eval plan grades recall, faithfulness, and trajectory. a barge-in during consent must show zero tools. nist measure is that test before any caller hears the bot. [cite:3] rollout is a release of a prompt hash, a model id, a tool allow-list, and an index build. shadow first, then a named queue, then a kill switch that returns the call to humans. check your hop traces for a millisecond target; it varies with the edge. check the tenant routing config for a dial-plan id; it varies by site. product families you may name are the ones already fetched: webex ai agent, amazon connect with q in connect, google ccai through the webex article, and dynamics 365 copilot as the learn pages describe it. article paths are not a walk of the lab tenant. [cite:4] [cite:5] note why it matters for the lab engineer the lab engineer is fictional. interviewers ask him to design a voice agent in forty-five minutes and then punish the design that has no queue, no abstention, and no rollback. this room is that answer written down: what is retrieved, who executes, how you know it failed, and how you turn it off without inventing the tenant’s menus. h 02architecture p caller to queue, with retrieval and a host between the model and any side effect. p diagram: contact path from caller through retrieval and a guarded model to either an answer or a human queue p read left to right. the platform answers the phone. the bot is a destination the platform can leave. retrieval returns passages or an empty pack. the model may speak from the pack or request a tool. the host checks the request. a tool result, not a draft sentence, is what the caller eventually hears when money or identity is involved. transfer builds a packet and returns the leg to the queue. assist, if you add it, is a second listener on the human’s desktop. it is not this picture’s speaker. p a grounded turn: retrieve, abstain or answer, and transfer when the pack or the policy says so. p diagram: caller, retriever, model, host, and queue exchanging a grounded answer or a transfer p the sequence is the happy path and the honest miss on one diagram. an empty pack does not call a refund tool to “be helpful.” it says it does not know, or it transfers. lewis et al. is why retrieval and generation are different stages. their 2020 scores are historical. the split is the part you keep. [cite:6] h 03deep dive p a capstone that only redraws t3 or only redraws t7 has dodged the interview. the work is the joints. retrieval can be right and the voice loop can still play a sentence from the wrong hop. the voice loop can be fast and the index can still be stale. the eval can be green on text and blind to barge-in. the rollout can “go to ten percent” without a kill switch. this room writes the joints. h the smallest bot that is still a design p scope it before you name a model. the smallest defensible bot answers from a published knowledge pack: hours, addresses, and policy sentences that already exist as articles. it does not refund. it does not collect a card. it transfers when the pack misses, when the caller asks for a person, or when consent would be required for a tool you have not built yet. containment is not resolution. you will report transfers and repeats beside any containment number. this room does not publish the acd’s reason-code catalog. log pack miss, caller asked, and policy refusal. p name the product family from a page, the way t7-r02 does. webex ai agent, scripted, voice, hours article only, is a design. connect self_service for the same article, with knowledge in one of the connectors the enablement page lists, is a design. a dynamics customer assist agent for high-volume voice, handing off with scrubbed history, is a design. “we will use ai” is not. do not claim dynamics is an amazon connect knowledge connector. the enablement page’s list was s3, sharepoint online, salesforce, servicenow, and zendesk. The citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date.</p></aside><p>One design, end to end: a caller asks a question, a retriever packs evidence, a model may request a tool, and a human queue still exists. This room is the architecture, the eval plan, and the rollout. It does not invent a dial plan, a word-error rate, or a millisecond promise.</p><h3>01Executive summary</h3><ul><li>The architecture is a cascade you can point at: media edge, retrieval, a model that may request a tool, a host that executes, and an ACD that still owns the route. Speech-to-speech collapses some hops. It does not delete the queue. [cite:1]</li><li>Grounding follows the embeddings guide: if the packed articles do not contain the answer, say you do not know. One embedding model per index. Hybrid search is T3-R04, not a feeling that “vectors are enough.” [cite:2]</li><li>The eval plan grades recall, faithfulness, and trajectory. A barge-in during consent must show zero tools. NIST Measure is that test before any caller hears the bot. [cite:3]</li><li>Rollout is a release of a prompt hash, a model id, a tool allow-list, and an index build. Shadow first, then a named queue, then a kill switch that returns the call to humans. Check your hop traces for a millisecond target; it varies with the edge. Check the tenant routing config for a dial-plan id; it varies by site.</li><li>Product families you may name are the ones already fetched: Webex AI Agent, Amazon Connect with Q in Connect, Google CCAI through the Webex article, and Dynamics 365 Copilot as the Learn pages describe it. Article paths are not a walk of the lab tenant. [cite:4] [cite:5]</li></ul><aside class="callout note"><h3>Why it matters for the lab engineer</h3><p>the lab engineer is fictional. Interviewers ask him to design a voice agent in forty-five minutes and then punish the design that has no queue, no abstention, and no rollback. This room is that answer written down: what is retrieved, who executes, how you know it failed, and how you turn it off without inventing the tenant’s menus.</p></aside><h3>02Architecture</h3><p>Caller to queue, with retrieval and a host between the model and any side effect.</p><p>Diagram: Contact path from caller through retrieval and a guarded model to either an answer or a human queue</p><p>Read left to right. The platform answers the phone. The bot is a destination the platform can leave. Retrieval returns passages or an empty pack. The model may speak from the pack or request a tool. The host checks the request. A tool result, not a draft sentence, is what the caller eventually hears when money or identity is involved. Transfer builds a packet and returns the leg to the queue. Assist, if you add it, is a second listener on the human’s desktop. It is not this picture’s speaker.</p><p>A grounded turn: retrieve, abstain or answer, and transfer when the pack or the policy says so.</p><p>Diagram: Caller, retriever, model, host, and queue exchanging a grounded answer or a transfer</p><p>The sequence is the happy path and the honest miss on one diagram. An empty pack does not call a refund tool to “be helpful.” It says it does not know, or it transfers. Lewis et al. is why retrieval and generation are different stages. Their 2020 scores are historical. The split is the part you keep. [cite:6]</p><h3>03Deep dive</h3><p>A capstone that only redraws T3 or only redraws T7 has dodged the interview. The work is the joints. Retrieval can be right and the voice loop can still play a sentence from the wrong hop. The voice loop can be fast and the index can still be stale. The eval can be green on text and blind to barge-in. The rollout can “go to ten percent” without a kill switch. This room writes the joints.</p><h3>The smallest bot that is still a design</h3><p>Scope it before you name a model. The smallest defensible bot answers from a published knowledge pack: hours, addresses, and policy sentences that already exist as articles. It does not refund. It does not collect a card. It transfers when the pack misses, when the caller asks for a person, or when consent would be required for a tool you have not built yet. Containment is not resolution. You will report transfers and repeats beside any containment number. This room does not publish the ACD’s reason-code catalog. Log pack miss, caller asked, and policy refusal.</p><p>Name the product family from a page, the way T7-R02 does. Webex AI Agent, scripted, voice, hours article only, is a design. Connect SELF_SERVICE for the same article, with knowledge in one of the connectors the enablement page lists, is a design. A Dynamics Customer Assist Agent for high-volume voice, handing off with scrubbed history, is a design. “We will use AI” is not. Do not claim Dynamics is an Amazon Connect knowledge connector. The enablement page’s list was S3, SharePoint Online, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Zendesk. [cite:4] [cite:5] [cite:7]</p><aside class="callout note"><h3>Gotcha</h3><p>Agent Answers, on the Cisco CCAI article, is not applicable to the Webex Contact Center solution. Data centers named on that page are not a latency budget. If your design says “Google will do agent assist on Webex Contact Center,” you have not read the distinction. Virtual Agent–voice and Agent Answers are not interchangeable labels. [cite:8]</p></aside><h3>The index</h3><p>Pick one embedding model and write its name on the index. [cite:11]</p><p>Tools on this smallest bot are read-only: a lookup that returns an article id you already retrieved, or a transfer that carries the packet.
